messages:
matt: Quick summary - ran a 1h profiling pass on continuous-batcher + kernel auto-select against rtx-pool. Seeing a ~12% P50 regression for short sequences (~64 tokens) when KV-hit rate > 0.7. Flamegraphs + perf traces in the link: https://internal/redwood/perf/1766001234 :thinking_face:

matt: Key observations:
- kernel_selector flips to fp16 matmul path for some models even when int8 microkernels would be faster at small batch sizes
- batch assembly often emits a lot of single-request microbatches; prefetch delay seems to desync KV eviction signals
- token_budget_target currently 512 for the low-latency tier; lowering it reduces batch size but increases RPC wall-time

devin: Can you paste the small flamegraph snippet? curious where the time is going (KV lookup vs GEMM).

matt: pasted minimal trace below (cropped):

```
0.0s - continuous_batcher::assemble_batches
0.12s - kv_cache::lookup_hit
0.18s - kernel_selector::choose_fp16_gemm
0.45s - gemm_fp16::run
0.60s - overhead/context_switch
```

matt: Notice choose_fp16_gemm called before we observe batch_size. selector is using estimated FLOPs from token_count only, not the actual assembled batch width.

chen: I dug into the selector logs from the canary node. snippet from kernel log: `selector: model=opt-2.7b est_ops=1.2e9 prefer_fp16=true batch_hint=1` - that batch_hint=1 is coming from a per-request cost hint set at enqueue time. we set that hint when prefetching starts; if prefetch is delayed, hint becomes stale and small.

chen: quick workaround: update selector to consult live_assembled_batch_size when available (best-effort) and only fallback to hint otherwise. patch ready: https://git.redwood/p/12345

matt: Nice. Two other levers I want to discuss: 1) token_budget_target bump (512->768) to reduce single-item microbatches for low-latency pool, 2) soft admit lease per-connection: let connections hold a token lease (200 tokens) for 50ms to allow small burst accumulation instead of immediate microbatch flush.

sara: Token bump increases latency variance for individual small requests though. For Dedicated customers we prefer deterministic tails. Maybe make token_budget_target dynamic per-tier: low-latency -> 768 but with max_batch_delay_ms=25, dedicated -> 512 and max_batch_delay_ms=10.

devin: Agree with chen's live-assembled-size consult + sara's dynamic target. Also propose adding a KV-hit multiplier: when KV_hit_rate > 0.6 allow token_budget_target += 20% because KV hits reduce kernel work. That might recover your P50 without adding tail latency.

matt: Good idea. We can compute kv_hit_rate as a rolling 30s EWMA per-host. I'll add multiplier logic in selector.

perf-bot: automated-report: canary nodes (3/3) show p50 up 11.8%, p95 flat, throughput -1.2% over 1h when token_budget_target=512 and selector_unpatched. Full logs: s3://redwood/perf/1766001234/canary.tar.gz

chen: small reproduce script for local: run `./bin/bench --model opt-2.7b --seq 64 --qps 150 --kv-hit 0.75 --prefetch-delay 20ms` - this creates the same microbatch pattern.

matt: Thanks. I'll land selector patch + dynamic token target PRs: p/12345 (selector live-size), p/12346 (dynamic-budget + kv-multiplier), plan canary rollout tonight with the following change set: token_budget_target(default)=512 -> per-tier override + kv multiplier, selector consult live batch size.

sara: For the soft-429/reject policy: if we allow slightly larger batching under high-KV-hit, we should also adjust admission soft limit to prefer serving small tokens from cached responses rather than queueing them in backpressure. Proposed text: "when kv_hit_rate > 0.6 and host_load < 85% allow speculative-join for up to 50ms; otherwise apply standard soft-429".

devin: Edge-case: that speculative-join can increase memory pressure if many clients hold leases. We should cap per-host speculative_tokens_outstanding <= 8k.

matt: noted. I'll add lease caps + eviction bump in the branch. Also adding metrics: per-host speculative_tokens, kv_hit_rate, live_assembled_batch_size, kernel_path_mismatch_count.

chen: LGTM on selector PR. also file an ops alert if kernel_path_mismatch_count > 50/min so we can rollback quickly.

matt: Plan for tonight: 1) merge selector change + metrics 2) feature flag dynamic-budget + kv-multiplier 3) canary 10% -> monitor p50/p95, kernel_path_mismatch_count 4) if mismatch spikes rollback selector only.

sara: +1. please include runbook steps for rollback in the PR description.

matt: Will do. Thanks all. ping me if you want to review the canary dashboard before rollout. :rocket:

devin: I'll run the local reproduce and send a short flamegraph overlay tomorrow AM.

perf-bot: note: alert suppression window set for 2h around the rollout.
